- YAML configuration will be imported to a ConfigEntry
- this will change default entity_ids and might break some customizations, automations and assignments to the energy dashboard for previous users. Since the integration now provides entities with unique_ids it can be changed back to the previous value if desired. 

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
This is a drop-in replacement of the current Fronius integration. 
This integration now
- provides a ConfigFlow
- doesn't need any other configuration than the IP address or hostname of the Fronius device
- provides an import for the now deprecated yaml config
- uses DataUpdateCoordinators
- creates entities with unique_ids
- assigns entities to devices
- uses SensorEntityDescription
- provides nearly all datapoints the old integration had (except for some omitted entities providing timestamp data of results which are always request time +- some milliseconds)
- is fully type annotated

pr_comments:
Hey there @nielstron, mind taking a look at this pull request as it has been labeled with an integration (`fronius`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L180) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

I tried the config flow at home and it seems to work perfectly fine. One thing that I did not understand yet: why did you decide to make all Sensor descriptions explicit? Was the pattern matching before too error prone? This way, you need to make sure that all possible sensor values returned by the fronius bridge are caught and displayed.

I just wanted to be able to set nice default names.
```python
"energy_reactive_ac_consumed": SensorEntityDescription(
        key="energy_reactive_ac_consumed",
        name="Energy Reactive AC consumed",
    )
```
and using this I found that expanding it to a full SensorEntityDescription was a nice way to have everything at one place so it is easy to reason about. This also makes sure proper HA supported unit constants are used (this is probably a bad example as `varh` isn't one of them 🤣).
```python
"energy_reactive_ac_consumed": SensorEntityDescription(
        key="energy_reactive_ac_consumed",
        name="Energy Reactive AC consumed",
        native_unit_of_measurement=ENERGY_VOLT_AMPERE_REACTIVE_HOUR,
        state_class=STATE_CLASS_TOTAL_INCREASING,
        icon="mdi:lightning-bolt-outline",
    )
```
Pattern matching this key for "energy*" would have wrongly set its `device_class=DEVICE_CLASS_ENERGY` leading to log errors
```log
WARNING (Recorder) [homeassistant.components.sensor.recorder] sensor.energy_reactive_ac_consumed_fronius_meter_0_http_10_1_2_5 has unknown unit VArh
```

Having the used keys explicit also enables to use others as `extra_state_attribute` like "meter_location" and "enable" from a meter device. I also deliberately excluded the "timestamp" key as I don't see a point in tracking the time in multiple entities.
![Bildschirmfoto 2021-09-13 um 23 21 12](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12422879/133158112-8cd87f7d-9919-401f-9363-c7c428b420d5.png)

The downside, as you said, is that pyfronius and the HA integration have to be in sync regarding newly added returned keys.

I just noticed that this drops support for Fronius Logger Info, which is available on most devices and provides useful data like the current energy price. Please do re-add that sensor (or add a note for this in the description)

> Pattern matching this key for "energy*" would have wrongly set its device_class=DEVICE_CLASS_ENERGY leading to log errors

Actually, the unit for reactive energy is not watt-hour precisely so that it is not confused with any actual power production (see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_power#Active,_reactive,_apparent,_and_complex_power_in_sinusoidal_steady-state). I think the device class Energy and non-watt-hour units should not necessarily result in a log error (this is more of a note towards the homeassistant dev team (@balloob ?) to allow certain non-watt-hour units for the device class energy).

> I think the device class Energy and non-watt-hour units should not necessarily result in a log error.

They do. I think because the recorder can't convert the units at some point https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/aaa62dadec4ccc019feec797346d412a0a565ace/homeassistant/components/sensor/recorder.py#L82
`DEVICE_CLASS_ENERGY` may only be set for entities with unit Wh or kWh. See also https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor

I deliberately left out Logger info for now because it only adds values that are constants which have to be set in the inverters Web-UI by the user. I think the least users have even set this, let alone keep this up to date. Keep in mind this is not the price information set and used in Solar.web 🙄

As, at least in my system, I sometimes get Timeouts from the Datalogger (in their Status code "LN-timeout" whatever that means) I tried to keep the request volume low. (this also happens with the current integration and is a Fronius issue). 

My plan was to extend the integration with an option flow later so users can set individual update intervals for the devices. Then I could imagine to add logger info with a default interval of 1 hour - 1 day instead of 1 minute like the other endpoints.
That said, if you think it's useful I can add it, no problem. I can just use a constant 1 hour scan interval for now...

> I deliberately left out Logger info for now because it only adds values that are constants which have to be set in the inverters Web-UI by the user. I think the least users have even set this, let alone keep this up to date. Keep in mind this is not the price information set and used in Solar.web roll_eyes

I see. The PR description just said that this would transfer *all* the sensors that were there before except for timestamp, which is simply incorrect right now.

I think that adding the logger is good, even if the user did not take care of it before it would be a good opportunity to remind the user of it. The upcoming versions of home assistant will provide options to monitor the price of energy where the information provided by logger info becomes especially interesting.

Oops, I forgot about this in the description 😬

I'll add a coordinator for the logger tonight. What do you think about 1 hour update interval?
If the values provided are really only user-managed and not dynamically updated by the system I think 1 hour (or less) updates sound reasonable.

I have included a logger_coordinator now. 

The returned data from Fronius looks like this:
```json
"delivery_factor": {
    "value": 0.15000000596046448,
    "unit": "EUR/kWh"
},
```
Unfortunately there are some pitfalls:
- Fronius does a bad job at converting floats so we receive `0.15000000596046448` for what is set to `0.15` in their web UI.
- the unit "EUR/kWh" is not device_class "monetary" compatible - it should be only EUR (or whatever currency) for that I think. I used the returned unit for now and didn't set a device_class. We could change the unit in pyfronius if we wanted to have the device_class set.
- I have no idea where "co2_factor" comes from. I can't find it in the web ui of my device but get a value returned 🤷‍♂️

> Fronius does a bad job at converting floats so we receive 0.15000000596046448 for what is set to 0.15 in their web UI.

That is true. I recall that some rounding was implemented in the homeassistant fronius before because of the slight imprecision caused by fronius doubles.

> the unit "EUR/kWh" is not device_class "monetary" compatible - it should be only EUR (or whatever currency) for that I think. I used the returned unit for now and didn't set a device_class. We could change the unit in pyfronius if we wanted to have the device_class set.

when I tried last EUR/kWh could be handled by the energy dashboard... I didn't assign a special device class I think

> I recall that some rounding was implemented in the homeassistant fronius before

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/30c25d44485cb3002d171f43049a5fa168bd2d40/homeassistant/components/fronius/sensor.py#L345

I think this is a bit unfortunate, because eg. grid tariffs can have more decimals than 2 - my export tariff for example is 0,076 €/kWh which would yield very different results when rounded to 2.
Should we do the rounding in pyfronius? There we could do it more granular and I think it fits since it is a Fronius issue.

The issue might stem from the underlying demjson to use the Decimal class rather than float to parse numbers. Could you try what happens if we use float instead of round? Otherwise, would 4 digits be a reasonable number of digits for any value?

> the underlying demjson to use the Decimal class rather than float to parse numbers

Where is that used?
I guess using `float()` yields the same as a `curl <IP>/GetLoggerInfo.cgi` also results in this rounding errored values. 

I think 4 digits sound reasonable. Will try how many decimals the web Ui even allows to configure there. 
Should we only do the rounding at LoggerSensor classes? All other classes values seem reasonable.

Whoops, mixed that up (its used in pysyncthru, not pyfronius). Checking the configurable precision in the Web UI is a good idea. And yeah, I agree that all other values seem good but I recall that this issue was present before the introduction of the Logger Info class.

So the web-UI saves up to 3 decimals (and rounds if I enter more). 
`power_flow` also reports eg. `"P_Load" : -1209.5599999999995,` 
so I guess rounding everything to 4 digits would be ok.

I still think this would be better handled in `pyfronius` since in HA we would have to check if it was a float, int, a string or boolean - in pyfronius we are extracting the values one-by-one anyway.

So I've added the rounding here, turned out to fit pretty nicely. 

@nielstron would you, as the codeowner, approve the overall changes or is something still missing / not appropriate?

That's right. I'll add a note to the PR description. 
Thank you!

you write "Since the integration now provides entities with unique_ids it can be changed back to the previous value if desired."

But why not do that automatically when you import the configuration.yaml ?

Hi 👋!
The new entity_id look like this: `sensor.energy_total`
Vs. the old entity_ids looked like this:
```
sensor.energy_total_fronius_inverter_1_http_10_1_2_6
       |            |       |        | |_ url
       |            |       |        |_ solarnet id
       |            |       |_ device type
       |            |_ domain
       |_ key
```
Seeing this now I'm not particular happy with either. 
- the new ones are kind of sparse - they should probably at least contain the domain. Is there a common practice for this? maybe `sensor.fronius_inverter_1_energy_total` (so they at least appear next to each other in dropdown menus)?
- it was a common (for a ~330 users) complaint in the community forums that the old style entity_ids were too long and cumbersome - therefore some users chose a custom component from HACS over the core component.
- the old style included the URL, which is probably not a good idea for the same reasons URLs are not applicable for unique_ids - if the URL changes the entity_id contains an IP address of a probably unrelated device
- the old ones practically contained every configuration key (device, sensor_type, scope) - these are not used anymore for meter and storage (system scope API endpoints are now always used instead of individual or system scope) so it would be a little cumbersome to recreate.

> But why not do that automatically when you import the configuration.yaml ?

We don't know which entities were used because they were (and still are) added dynamically as values appear in API responses and they have not had a unique_id so nothing entity_registry entry.

Can't really make up my mind about that. I'm open for suggestions.

I agree that the old naming scheme is very clunky and not really consistent with other integrations. 
Why not introduce a name when setting up the config flow (default can be the url) and then do
my_name_energy_total

I like the idea of a configurable name, but I'm not sure if adding it to the entity_id is a good idea because changing the name later would unexpectedly either change or not change the associated entity_ids (depending on a users expectations which I guess vary 🙃 in that case).

@farmio it would certainly make sense for the display name to use the name configured in **Fronius** itself, but the unique ID could be prefixed with the host. I unfortuantely cannot find any of the APIs that give the name configured in Fronius though.
This PR needs to be broken down into multiple PRs. We should not accept big overhauls like this, covering multiple feature changes, in a single PR.
The dependency update is now done and already merged in #57279
Well there is a version now that only includes the move to DataUpdateCoordinator and addition of unique_id #57879
closed in favor of #59686

issue_context.title: Fronius GEN 24 not getting produced energy data
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I'm using a Fronius GEN24 inverter with smart meter and supported battery. The electrician tells me this is a quite new model. 
The integration works fine, except for the energy reports, that remain unknown. Maybe the interface or the APIs changed a little, I don't know how that value is obtained by the integration. 
Let me know how to provide help in troubleshooting and figuring out how to get it right. 

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021-7-4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Core

### Integration causing the issue

Fronius

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/fronius/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
I used the basic config in the documentation for an installation with smart meter and battery and it worked just fine.
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>

Hey there @nielstron, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`fronius`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L179) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

This is most likely a problem of the underlying package, https://github.com/nielstron/pyfronius

You can try to run the package manually and see which values are returned :) If your value is not among them, you'd need to try to find  out which API call returns the correct values on the fronius device.

Sorry, I don't have experience in phyton, but I'd be glad to help in posting the result if you can point me the right way: exactly which command I have to send?
Also, I don't have a phyton environment on the PC, can I use the raspberry that's running home assistant?

You can technically use the raspberry that is running home assistant. For that you would need to be able to log into it and use the home assistant virtual environment. Other than that, setting up the project on your PC should be fairly easy. Just install Python, and via pip the package "pyfronius".

Then you can run the script https://github.com/nielstron/pyfronius/blob/master/example.py like this
```bash
python3 example.py FRONIUS-URL
```

Do the values not turn up anywhere in home assistant or just don't make it to the energy dashboard? It seems very unlikely to me that no sensor at all are generated for these values (if the correct device class was added)

- sensor.entry_day_fronius_power_flow_0
- sensor.entry_year_fronius_power_flow_0
- sensor.entry_total_fronius_power_flow_0 

are there but empty which is to be expected from the parsed values above.

no sensors for :

- energy_real_consumed
- energy_real_produced

What do you mean exactly  by 'correct device class was added'?

This is my config:

```
- platform: fronius
    # name: Symo GEN24 Plus
    resource: http://192.168.179.45
    monitored_conditions:
    - sensor_type: inverter
      device: 1
      scope: device
    - sensor_type: meter
      device: 3
      scope: device
    - sensor_type: storage
      device: 0
    - sensor_type: power_flow
```

I can confirm: I have an auto-entities card configured like this:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37505492/128469807-a09cac36-840f-43da-bd69-5955e020ad4c.png)
and I get 3 energy sensors, all unavailable:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37505492/128469857-82873923-536d-423d-8312-3598f72f7951.png)

> What do you mean exactly by 'correct device class was added'?

I meant you to check whether the scope and device in the home assistant config match what you are manually polling in pyfronius.
(that is, what is suggested in this thread: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/54047#issuecomment-893883513)

That solved my problem of not getting the meter measurements.
 My meter needed to be configured as device 0.
Thank you very much for your support.

That fixed it for me too. I'd never have guessed that the meter had a problem since the addon was correctly reporting what I thought was "meter" data such as energy consumed by the house.
Now I must ask: is there a way to know what are the devide_ID in advance (that should be added in the HA docs too...
Thanks for your help, I think the issue can be closed now.

EDIT: In fact maybe it should be left open: I now can see energy readings form the meter, but still can't see the "power flow" from the inverter as I previously posted.
I can see these:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37505492/128517763-57f64503-86ea-41e0-a127-a3bec9bd7203.png)
but still can't see these:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37505492/128517832-56723eed-be0c-49b1-a7ea-a9f901b21333.png)

> Now I must ask: is there a way to know what are the devide_ID in advance (that should be added in the HA docs too...

Not sure how that works actually.. But it makes me think, maybe I can just configure the integration to probe all devices and just measure every possible sensor.
Also, some energy counters by Fronius are still in Wh. Could you output everything in KWh as expected by HA energy dashboard?

Looking at https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor/#properties it seems to me that "Wh" is a perfectly supported unit in HA energy measurements. Where does it say that only kWh is accepted for the dashboard?

I thought they said to target kWh as unit on the last release party. But if Wh is fine per documentation I guess it should work.
Nevertheless who measures their energy usage in Wh? Maybe caravan drivers with 150W solar and lead batteries :)
The energy providers certainly not. Imho it should be all about being the most intuitive for the majority of users.

Well it's the default measurement unit of the fronius device. So I prefer to keep it that way.

I have tested it on the dev branch and their Wh works.

The measurements are rounded to the kWh, everything less than 1kWh is shown as 0kWh, everything less than 2kWh is shown as 1kWh.
Fronius inverters IG + datamanager

`-   platform: fronius
    resource: http://192.168.1.102
    scan_interval: 10
    monitored_conditions:
    - sensor_type: inverter
      scope: device
-   platform: fronius
    resource: http://192.168.1.103

> The integration works fine, except for the energy reports, that remain unknown.

What exactly do you mean by that? Which sensors show up in the dashboard and which not? which ones can you choose among in the energy dashboard?

Hello, I have a question, which is most probably related to the same issue.

@Toffi32 The requested changes will be part of the upcoming version of home assistant.

Hello,
I'm running the current beta(core-2021.9.0b1), but sadly it's not yet working.
At the moment I can only select the total day,year, total measurements ( which are "Unknown"). The real/current power are not available for selection.

![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3853374/131113602-de4f9e62-b60d-4566-85ac-ea9267515bd7.png)

> The real/current power are not available for selection.

This is because energy (Wh "Arbeit") is needed for the energy panel. Power (W "Leistung") is not supported by the energy panel.

You'd need the entities from `meter`, not `power_flow`.

Exactly, I simply added some integration platform sensors that keep track of the energy:
 - platform: integration
   source: sensor.power_photovoltaics_fronius_power_flow_0_http_192_168_0_158
   name: fv_energia_prodotta
   unit_prefix: k
   round: 2

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37505492/131154523-e1b32baf-df8d-423a-923f-23837a923598.png)

@tigers75 `inverter` and `meter` provide suitable entities without the need for manual integration (and thus provide more accurate values when HA has had no connection for for some time for whatever reason).
Yes, I know mine is a temporary workaround, I was pointing it out for who's not getting the data in the energy panel.

The new Fronius GEN24 inverters don't have internal production counters (yet). They can only sum up the production in solar web so far. In that case the summation via energy counter is needed. Don't forget to set the device_class: energy via customize to persist it.

Have any of you gotten the new energy battery integration to work with a fronius controlled battery?

I have achieved it like this:
```
- platform: template
  sensors:
    power_discharging_the_battery:
      unique_id: power_discharging_the_battery
      value_template: >-
        {% set power = states('sensor.power_battery_fronius_power_flow_0_http_192_168_179_45') | float %}
        {% if power > 0.0 %} {{ states('sensor.power_battery_fronius_power_flow_0_http_192_168_179_45')|float }}
        {% else %} 0.0 {% endif %}
      device_class: power
      unit_of_measurement: "W"
    power_charging_the_battery:
      unique_id: power_charging_the_battery
      value_template: >-
        {% set power = states('sensor.power_battery_fronius_power_flow_0_http_192_168_179_45') | float %}
        {% if power < 0.0 %} {{ (states('sensor.power_battery_fronius_power_flow_0_http_192_168_179_45')|float * -1) }}
        {% else %} 0.0 {% endif %}
      device_class: power
      unit_of_measurement: "W"

- platform: integration
  source: sensor.power_discharging_the_battery
  name: energy_discharged_from_the_battery
  method: left

- platform: integration
```

Does this work? My understanding is that this will set the native value on init only. I would expect you should just rename the `_get_entity_value` function to `native_value`.

Famous last words: It works fine on my system 🤣

The entities are instantiated after instantiating the coordinator, so `_handle_coordinator_update()` is not called after an entity is created and would not have an init value then. Later updates are handled by `_handle_coordinator_update()`

Since we can't be sure if the key is contained in the latest API response (`coordinator.data` dict) the state would turn to `None` instead of stay on the latest known value. This happens eg. after sunset when an inverter doesn't produce anymore - Fronius API just omits some keys then 🙄

Actually, the state turning to None is not a problem. This is the intended way of telling HA that the current state could not be fetched. AFAIK HA will still display the latest non-None retrieved value.
